Holiest
hō´lĭ-ĕst
n. (the Holiest of all; the inner sanctuary behind the second veil — Greek hagia hagion)
The superlative of holy, rendering the Hebrew idiom holy of holies — the Semitic way of forming a superlative by doubling the noun.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The Holiest is the innermost room of the sanctuary, and the epistle to the Hebrews is built around who may enter it. “After the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all” (Heb 9:3) — behind that veil stood the ark, and into it the high priest went alone, once a year, not without blood. The writer draws the lesson the arrangement was designed to teach: “The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing” (Heb 9:8). The closed veil was itself a sermon: access was not yet open, and the annual repetition proved that nothing had been finished. Then the conclusion the whole epistle exists to reach: “Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh” (Heb 10:19-20). Every term is deliberate. Boldness, where once there was exclusion; to enter, and not merely to approach; by the blood of Jesus, and by nothing else; a way that is new and living, because the Priest who opened it is alive; and the veil is His flesh, torn from the top down when He died.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines the holy of holies as the innermost apartment of the Jewish tabernacle and temple, where the ark was kept, and into which the high priest alone entered once a year.

HO'LIEST, a. superlative of holy; most holy.

HOLY OF HOLIES, the innermost apartment of the Jewish tabernacle and temple, called also the most holy place.

VEIL, n. A cover; a curtain; in the temple, the hanging that separated the holy place from the most holy.

BOLD'NESS, n. Confidence; courage; liberty of access and of speech.

Key Scripture

Hebrews 10:19 — "Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus,"

Hebrews 10:20 — "By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;"

Hebrews 9:3 — "And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all;"

Hebrews 9:8 — "The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing:"

Modern Corruption

A human priesthood is reintroduced between the believer and God, or else access is assumed on terms other than the blood, and both empty the torn veil of meaning.

expand to see more

Hebrews 10:19 is the death of every sacerdotal system. The boldness to enter the holiest belongs to brethren — the whole company of believers — and the ground is the blood of Jesus, offered once. Where a church interposes a mediating priesthood, repeats a sacrifice, or makes access depend on a man's absolution, it has rebuilt the veil that God tore from the top downward at the ninth hour. Hebrews argues the point at length: those priests were many because death forbade them to continue, and they offered daily because nothing was ever finished; this Man, after He had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down.

The opposite error assumes access without reckoning what it cost. Nothing in these chapters supports a casual approach; the same epistle says our God is a consuming fire, and the boldness it grants is granted with the price named in the same sentence — by the blood of Jesus, through a veil that is His flesh. A worshipper who has understood Hebrews 9 comes into the holiest with confidence and with awe together, and the two are not in competition. He enters where the high priest trembled to go once a year, and he enters because Another went in first and did not come out to repeat it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek hagia hagion, holy of holies — Hebrews 9:3; ta hagia, the holy places — Hebrews 9:8, 10:19; Hebrew qodesh haqqodashim, the most holy place; parresia (G3954), boldness of access.

expand to see more

Greek hagia hagion — holy of holies; Hebrews 9:3, rendering the Hebrew superlative idiom.

Greek parresia (G3954) — boldness, freedom of speech and access; Hebrews 10:19, Ephesians 3:12, 1 John 4:17.

Greek prosphatos (G4372) — new, freshly slain; Hebrews 10:20, the new and living way.

Hebrew qodesh haqqodashim — the most holy place; Exodus 26:33-34, entered once a year with blood.

Matthew 27:51 records the veil of the temple rent in twain from the top to the bottom at the moment He died.

Usage

"“Boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus” — addressed to brethren."

"“The way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest” — the closed veil preached."

"“Through the veil, that is to say, his flesh”."
